headline: High risk: Open Interpreter’s default filesystem/clipboard/code-execution surfaces can ingest MemMachine outputs and turn them into unsafe actions or leaks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine can expose outputs through REST/Python SDK/MCP, and Open Interpreter can consume clipboard/files/stdin with no default isolation. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MemMachine content is copied or routed into Open Interpreter. The pairwise pathway is documented by profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or files
IF Open Interpreter parses MemMachine-generated text as instructions without a provenance filter
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Route MemMachine output through a plain-text sanitizer
Require a human review step before Open Interpreter executes any imported text
Use Open Interpreter in Docker or another isolated environment
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress. If MemMachine outputs are passed into Open Interpreter, sensitive context can be exposed to local files, shell commands, or external model providers. The blast radius is broad and the default Open Interpreter posture is unsafe.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores or emits user preferences into files or prompts consumed by Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter sends those prompts or files to configured model providers
mitigations: Keep MemMachine outputs out of shared filesystems
Disable or restrict Open Interpreter network egress
Run Open Interpreter with a separate OS account and minimal file access
Redact long-term user facts before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and API, while Open Interpreter can write files, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same workspace, they can race on shared mutable state and corrupt files or commits. The profiles explicitly show filesystem-based shared state for Open Interpreter, so the conflict is plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Open Interpreter runs with write access while MemMachine emits file-backed artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared state
Use git branches and explicit commit locks
Restrict Open Interpreter to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add workspace locking and transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can generate context-rich outputs, and Open Interpreter can act on text by executing shell or modifying files. If Open Interpreter treats MemMachine output as authoritative, a mistaken plan or hallucinated fact can cascade into real actions. The pairwise interaction is plausible, but verification is not enabled by default.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is fed MemMachine-generated instructions or plans
IF no human verification step occurs before execution
mitigations: Require confirmation for every action block
Insert a fact-check step before execution
Limit Open Interpreter to dry-run mode for MemMachine outputs
Have MemMachine emit structured data instead of free-form instructions
requires-engineering: add automated validation of downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is a travel-planning agent that stores long-term user facts, while Open Interpreter can access the entire local machine and send data to configured model providers. If travel data includes personal or location-sensitive information, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through local files and external API calls. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF travel-related personal data is stored in MemMachine and then processed by Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter forwards that data to a third-party model provider or retains it on disk
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts or files
Configure shorter retention for Open Interpreter logs
Use a local-only model provider for sensitive sessions
Separate EU/regulated data from general desktop automation
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
